captions.text: Recap of chapter 19: word search failed when a question avoided the document's words.
So you turned text into vectors, and compared them with cosine.
VectorStore keeps the vectors, and Index embeds and searches.
You found the right file, but you still don't have an answer.
Today's black box: answering from documents.
Let's open it. But first, try the simplest idea.
Paste the whole handbook into the prompt, and ask two questions.
Both facts are in the handbook. Predict: will the model get both right?
The shoe allowance is right. Pasting seems to work.
But it says E44 isn't there. It is, in grinder-errors.md.
Five runs each: shoes 5 of 5, E44 0 of 5. It never named its file either.
There was no error. So measure the handbook, one file at a time.
4,764 tokens. But tokens_in said 2,050. Ollama cut it, and said nothing.
The start went, and the instructions went with it.
The fix is one option: num_ctx sets the size of the window.
Predict: what will tokens_in be at 8192?
5,080 tokens, and 15 of 15. Same model, same text.
Now add a year of records. Together that's 69,872 tokens, in 95 files.
The model's limit is 32,768. Predict: how much gets in at that limit?
Just 16,386 tokens, 23% of the text. Only the last files survived.
Each question ran once, so it's a sample. But the wall is real.
You can't send everything, so you must choose. First, cut the documents up.
Split at blank lines, and collect paragraphs in current.
When the next paragraph would pass size, the piece is finished.
Predict: how many pieces will each of these give?
Three, two and one. A paragraph is never broken.
All 95 files make 934 chunks at size 60, and 447 at size 120.
This is the whole pipeline. Search once.
Put the hits in the prompt, with their file names.
Ask the model once. No loop, and no tools.
Now the flood, which pasting missed. Predict: how many tokens now?
It found the February log, and the answer names its file.
570 tokens, against 16,386 for pasting.
Flood 5 of 5. And it said I don't know about dental, 5 of 5.
A wrong answer could be the search or the model. So measure the search alone.
hit_rate checks the right file, not the right text. It's a file hit rate.
Predict: which index finds the most files?
Whole files lead at k=5, 31 to 28. So why chunk?
Score the answers: 42 questions, three runs each, and rag60 twice.
rag60 scored 99, then 100. rag120 scored 99. Don't pick a winner.
Whole files: the most files, and the lowest score, 74.
But look at none and records. It's the silent cut again.
So give whole files room: num_ctx 16384.
103 of 126, level with chunks. We expected chunks to win. They didn't.
The difference is cost: 7,191 tokens here, and 570 with chunks.
Does a file hit mean a right answer? Print where the two disagree.
Four found the file and still lost runs. One missed it and passed.
hair is a false failure: the right answer said tie, and our check wanted tied.
Tidewater's fee is £85, and the chunk holding it was found.
But its heading landed in the chunk before. The name nearby is Northline.
0 of 5. The file hit rate counts this as a success.
Is RAG always better? On the handbook, pasting can fit. Predict the winner.
Pasting at the default window: 38 of 96. The silent cut is the worst result.
Pasting with room beat RAG here, 83 to 75. RAG won only on gap.
If your documents fit, you may not need RAG. Always check tokens_in.
Your turn. Open exercises.py and complete the five TODOs.
There's also an optional exercise: paste everything, and report back.
You've finished when you see 5 passed.
